```{r data cleaning}
data2 <- data %>%
  filter(
    age >= 50,
    if_all(c(time, event, age, gender, race, BMI, CHD, TMIMS), ~ !is.na(.)),
    time > 0,
    CHD %in% c("Yes", "No")) %>% 
  ## create mortality time in years
  mutate(time = time/12,
         age_group = cut(age, 
                         breaks = seq(min(age, na.rm = TRUE), max(age, na.rm = TRUE) + 5, by = 10),
                         right = FALSE),
         MIMS_group = cut(TMIMS,
                          breaks = quantile(TMIMS, c(0, 0.333, 0.667, 1)), 
                          labels = c("low TMIMS", "medium TMIMS", "high TMIMS"),
                          include.lowest = TRUE))
data2$CHD <- droplevels(data2$CHD)
```

```{r data cleaning}
# define s_grid (length P)
# s_grid <- seq(1/60, 24, length = 1440)
s_grid <- seq(0, 1, len = 1440)

# survival outcome
time <- data2$time
status <- data2$event

# cluster id
cluster_id <- data2$STRAPSU

# functional covariate
X <- data2$MIMS
age <- data2$age

# scalar covariates design matrix Z
# Columns are: (Intercept), age_in_years, bmi
Z <- model.matrix(~ age + gender + BMI + CHD, data = data2)
# Z <- model.matrix(~ gender + BMI + CHD, data = data2)
```


```{r gibbs sampler}
### run Gibbs sampler
fit_bayes_int <- gibbs_frailty_interaction(
  time = time,
  status = status,
  cluster_id = cluster_id,
  Z = Z,
  X = X,
  age = age,
  s_grid = s_grid,
  # tuning / priors
  K_s = 10,
  K_age = 5,
  lambda_init = 5000,         
  A_lambda = 1, B_lambda = 0.001, 
  var_gamma = 100,
  A_tau2 = 3, B_tau2 = 2,
  A_sigma2 = 3, B_sigma2 = 2,
  # MCMC
  n_iter = 20000,
  n_burn = 10000,
  n_thin = 1,
  verbose = TRUE
)

```

```{r posterior summaries}
quantile(fit_bayes_int$sigma2, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
quantile(fit_bayes_int$tau2,   c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
hist(colMeans(fit_bayes_int$u))
```

```{r interaction surface}
reconstruct_interaction_surface <- function(mcmc_out, grid_age = seq(50, 80, by = 0.5), grid_s = s_grid) {
  require(mgcv)
  
  meta <- mcmc_out$meta
  sm_tensor <- meta$sm_tensor
  
  # 1. Create a dense evaluation grid
  eval_grid <- expand.grid(s_grid = grid_s, age = grid_age)
  
  # 2. Get the Prediction Matrix for the interaction
  # PredictMat handles the absorb.cons constraint internally
  Phi_pred <- PredictMat(sm_tensor, eval_grid)
  
  # 3. Calculate posterior draws of the surface
  # beta_surface_draws: (Number of MCMC Samples) x (Number of Grid Points)
  surface_draws <- mcmc_out$b %*% t(Phi_pred)
  
  # 4. Summarize (Mean and 95% Credible Intervals)
  eval_grid$beta_mean <- colMeans(surface_draws)
  eval_grid$lower     <- apply(surface_draws, 2, quantile, 0.025)
  eval_grid$upper     <- apply(surface_draws, 2, quantile, 0.975)
  
  return(eval_grid)
}

# Get the processed grid
plot_data <- reconstruct_interaction_surface(fit_bayes_int)
# Identify where the 95% CI does not contain zero
plot_data <- plot_data %>%
  mutate(is_significant = case_when(
    lower > 0 ~ 1,
    upper < 0 ~ 1,
    TRUE ~ 0
  ))

# Heatmap Visualization
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = s_grid, y = age)) +
  # Main Heatmap
  geom_tile(aes(fill = beta_mean)) +
  # Add black contour lines with a mapped aesthetic for the legend
  geom_contour(aes(z = is_significant, color = "Significant (95% CI)"), 
               breaks = 0.5, 
               linewidth = 0.5) +
  # Define the gradient for the heatmap
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0) +
  # Define the manual color for the contour legend
  scale_color_manual(name = "", values = c("Significant (95% CI)" = "black")) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25),
    labels = c('12 AM', '6 AM', '12 PM', '6 PM', '12 AM')
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Time of day (s)",
    y = "Age (years)",
    title = "K_s = 10, K_age = 8",
    fill = expression(beta(s, age))
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.box = "vertical", # Stacks the two legends
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  ) 

library(plotly)
library(tidyr)

# 1. Reshape the data into a matrix format
# We need s_grid as columns and age as rows
matrix_data <- plot_data %>%
  select(s_grid, age, beta_mean) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = s_grid, values_from = beta_mean) %>%
  column_to_rownames("age") %>%
  as.matrix()

# 2. Extract axis values
age_axis <- as.numeric(rownames(matrix_data))
s_grid_axis <- as.numeric(colnames(matrix_data))

# 3. Create the 3D surface
plot_ly(x = ~s_grid_axis, y = ~age_axis, z = ~matrix_data) %>%
  add_surface(
    colorscale = list(c(0, "blue"), c(0.5, "white"), c(1, "red")),
    colorbar = list(title = "beta(s, age)")
  ) %>%
  layout(
    title = "K_s = 10, K_age = 10",
    scene = list(
      xaxis = list(title = "Time of Day (s)", ticktext = c('12 AM', '6 AM', '12 PM', '6 PM', '12 AM'), tickvals = seq(0, 1, 0.25)),
      yaxis = list(title = "Age (years)"),
      zaxis = list(title = "Effect Size")
    )
  )
```

```{r}
# 1. Select the ages you want to compare
target_ages <- c(50, 55, 60, 65, 70, 75, 80)

# 2. Filter the reconstructed surface data
# Note: We find the closest available age in your grid to your targets
slice_data <- plot_data[plot_data$age %in% 
                          unique(plot_data$age)[sapply(target_ages, function(x) which.min(abs(unique(plot_data$age) - x)))], ]

# 3. Create the Slice Plot
ggplot(slice_data, aes(x = s_grid, y = beta_mean, color = as.factor(age), fill = as.factor(age))) +
  # geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  # Add a horizontal reference line at 0
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  # Match your requested X-axis formatting
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25),
    labels = c('12 AM', '6 AM', '12 PM', '6 PM', '12 AM')
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Comparison of activity effects by age",
    subtitle = "Slices of beta(s, age) with 95% credible intervals",
    x = "Time of day (s)",
    y = expression(beta(s, age)),
    color = "Age",
    fill = "Age"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r cross validation}
# 1. Initialization
n_folds <- 10

# Ensure tgrid is strictly positive for the Log-Normal AFT (start at 0.1, not 0)
tgrid <- seq(0.1, 8, len = 100) 

# ==========================================
# DEFINE THE TWO FOLD SETTINGS
# ==========================================
set.seed(916)

# --- Setting 1: Split by Cluster (STRAPSU) ---
# All subjects in a given cluster will go to the same fold.
unique_clusters <- unique(data2$STRAPSU)
# Randomly assign each unique cluster to a fold from 1 to 10
cluster_fold_assignments <- sample(rep(1:n_folds, length.out = length(unique_clusters)))
names(cluster_fold_assignments) <- as.character(unique_clusters)
# Map the cluster fold assignments back to the individual rows in data2
fold_setting1 <- unname(cluster_fold_assignments[as.character(data2$STRAPSU)])

# --- Setting 2: Split by Subject, Stratified by Cluster ---
# Subjects are split individually, but cluster proportions are maintained across folds.
# createFolds automatically stratifies when given a factor.
fold_setting2 <- caret::createFolds(as.factor(data2$STRAPSU), k = n_folds, list = FALSE)

# Group the settings into a list to loop through
cv_settings <- list(
  "Setting 1: Split whole dataset by cluster (STRAPSU)" = fold_setting1,
  "Setting 2: Split by individual subjects (Stratified by cluster)" = fold_setting2
)

# ==========================================
# MAIN OUTER LOOP FOR CV SETTINGS
# ==========================================

for (setting_name in names(cv_settings)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n\n********************************************************\n"))
  cat(sprintf("STARTING CROSS-VALIDATION: %s\n", setting_name))
  cat(sprintf("********************************************************\n"))
  
  # Get the fold assignments for the current setting
  fold <- cv_settings[[setting_name]]
  
  # Storage for the Integrated Brier Score (IBS) and C-index for each fold
  IBS_bayes  <- IBS_laft  <- IBS_lfcm  <- IBS_lfcmfr  <- rep(0, n_folds)
  Cidx_bayes <- Cidx_laft <- Cidx_lfcm <- Cidx_lfcmfr <- rep(0, n_folds)
  
  for (i in 1:n_folds) {
    cat(sprintf("\n--- Fold %d / %d ---\n", i, n_folds))
    
    # Split data
    train_idx <- which(fold != i)
    test_idx  <- which(fold == i)
    
    train_data <- data2[train_idx, ]
    test_data  <- data2[test_idx, ]
    
    # ==========================================
    # MODEL 1: Fit & Predict Bayesian lfAFT with frailty
    # ==========================================
    cat("Fitting lfAFT with frailty...\n")
    
    Z_train <- model.matrix(~ age + BMI + gender + CHD, data = train_data)
    X_train <- as.matrix(train_data$MIMS)
      
    Z_test  <- model.matrix(~ age + BMI + gender + CHD, data = test_data)
    X_test  <- as.matrix(test_data$MIMS)
      
    # Safely align columns (handles missing factor levels in the test fold)
    missing_cols <- setdiff(colnames(Z_train), colnames(Z_test))
      
    if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
      for (col in missing_cols) {
        Z_test <- cbind(Z_test, 0)               # Add column of zeros
        colnames(Z_test)[ncol(Z_test)] <- col    # Name it correctly
      }
    }
      
    # Reorder Z_test to perfectly match Z_train and drop any strictly novel levels
    Z_test <- Z_test[, colnames(Z_train), drop = FALSE]
    
    fit_bayes <- gibbs_frailty_interaction( 
      time       = train_data$time, 
      status     = train_data$event, 
      cluster_id = train_data$STRAPSU,
      Z          = Z_train, 
      X          = X_train, 
      age        = train_data$age,
      s_grid     = s_grid,
      K_s        = 10,
      K_age      = 5,
      n_iter     = 20000, 
      n_burn     = 10000,
      verbose    = FALSE 
    )
    
    pred_bayes <- predict_gibbs_interaction(
      fit            = fit_bayes,
      X_new          = X_test,
      Z_new          = Z_test,
      age_new        = test_data$age,
      cluster_id_new = test_data$STRAPSU,
      type           = "survival",
      times          = tgrid
    )
    
    S_bayes <- pred_bayes$mean
    
    # ==========================================
    # MODEL 2: Fit & Predict LFCM with frailty (fcoxFr)
    # ==========================================
    cat("Fitting LFCM with frailty...\n")
    X_train_mat <- matrix(X_train, ncol = 1440, byrow = FALSE)
    X_test_mat <- matrix(X_test, ncol = 1440, byrow = FALSE)
    fit_lfcmfr <- fpcr(time = train_data$time, event = train_data$event, group = train_data$STRAPSU,
                               X = X_train_mat, Z = Z_train[, -1], nb = 10, gp = s_grid)
    
    # Linear predictor for the train set
    pred_lfcmfr_train <- fpcr_predict(object = fit_lfcmfr, time = train_data$time, event = train_data$event,
                                      group = train_data$STRAPSU, X = X_train_mat, Z = Z_train[, -1])
    eta_train <- pred_lfcmfr_train$predictions
    
    # Linear predictor for the test set
    pred_lfcmfr_test <- fpcr_predict(object = fit_lfcmfr, time = test_data$time, event = test_data$event,
                                     group = test_data$STRAPSU, X = X_test_mat, Z = Z_test[, -1])
    eta_test <- pred_lfcmfr_test$predictions
    
    # Survival probability matrix
    S_lfcmfr <- get_breslow_survival(
      eta_train   = eta_train, 
      time_train  = train_data$time, 
      event_train = train_data$event, 
      eta_test    = eta_test, 
      tgrid       = tgrid
    )
    
    # ==========================================
    # MODEL 3: Fit & Predict lfAFT (funAFT)
    # ==========================================
    cat("Fitting lfAFT...\n")
    fit_laft <- fit_lfAFT(data = train_data, y = "time", delta = "event", x = "MIMS", x_as_regex = FALSE,
                          z = c("age", "BMI", "gender", "CHD"),
                          family = "lognormal", k = 10, basis = "cc", s_grid = s_grid, se = FALSE)
    
    S_laft <- predict_lfAFT(fit_laft, test_data, type  = "survival", times = tgrid)
    
    # ==========================================
    # MODEL 4: Fit & Predict LFCM (mgcv)
    # ==========================================
    cat("Fitting LFCM...\n")
    
    N <- nrow(train_data) # number of samples
    # Quadrature weights for Riemann integration
    lvec <- matrix(1 / 1440, 1440, 1)
    # matrix containing quadrature weights for all participants
    L <- kronecker(matrix(1, N, 1),t(lvec))
    # matrix containing functional domain values
    S <- kronecker(matrix(1, N, 1), t(s_grid))
    train_data$S <- I(S)
    #Pointwise product of w i(s) and the quadrature weights, "L"
    train_data$W_L <- I(train_data$MIMS * L)
  
    fit_lfcm <- gam(time ~ age + BMI + gender + CHD + 
                    s(S, by=W_L, bs="cc", k=1 0), 
                    method="REML", 
                    data=train_data, 
                    weights=train_data$event, # Assuming 'event' is the status indicator
                    family=cox.ph)
    
    N_test <- nrow(test_data) # number of test samples
    # Quadrature weights for Riemann integration
    L_test <- kronecker(matrix(1, N_test, 1),t(lvec))
    # matrix containing functional domain values
    S_test <- kronecker(matrix(1, N_test, 1), t(s_grid))
    test_data$S <- I(S_test)
    #Pointwise product of w i(s) and the quadrature weights, "L"
    test_data$W_L <- I(test_data$MIMS * L_test)
    
    # mgcv::cox.ph evaluates survival probability based on the 'time' column in newdata.
    # We loop over tgrid to build an (N_test x length(tgrid)) survival matrix.
    S_lfcm <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(test_data), ncol = length(tgrid))
    
    for(j in seq_along(tgrid)) {
      tmp_test <- test_data
      tmp_test$time <- tgrid[j] 
      S_lfcm[, j] <- predict(fit_lfcm, newdata = tmp_test, type = "response")
    }
    
    # ==========================================
    # METRICS: Calculate IPCW IBS and IPCW C-Index
    # ==========================================
    cat("Calculating IPCW Brier Scores and IPCW C-Index...\n")
    
    # --- 1. IPCW Integrated Brier Scores ---
    IBS_bayes[i]  <- cal_IPCW_Brier(S_mat = S_bayes, time_test = test_data$time, event_test = test_data$event, 
                                    time_train = train_data$time, event_train = train_data$event, tgrid = tgrid)
    IBS_lfcmfr[i] <- cal_IPCW_Brier(S_mat = S_lfcmfr, time_test = test_data$time, event_test = test_data$event, 
                                    time_train = train_data$time, event_train = train_data$event, tgrid = tgrid)
    IBS_laft[i]   <- cal_IPCW_Brier(S_mat = S_laft, time_test = test_data$time, event_test = test_data$event, 
                                    time_train = train_data$time, event_train = train_data$event, tgrid = tgrid)
    IBS_lfcm[i]   <- cal_IPCW_Brier(S_mat = S_lfcm, time_test = test_data$time, event_test = test_data$event, 
                                    time_train = train_data$time, event_train = train_data$event, tgrid = tgrid)
    
    # --- 2. Extracting Risk Scores ---
    risk_bayes  <- -rowSums(S_bayes)
    risk_lfcmfr <- eta_test
    risk_laft   <- -predict_lfAFT(fit_laft, test_data, type = "link")
    risk_lfcm   <- predict(fit_lfcm, newdata = test_data, type = "link")
    
    # --- 3. Uno's IPCW C-Index Calculation ---
    Surv_train <- Surv(train_data$time, train_data$event)
    Surv_test  <- Surv(test_data$time, test_data$event)
    
    Cidx_bayes[i]  <- UnoC(Surv.rsp = Surv_train, Surv.rsp.new = Surv_test, lpnew = risk_bayes)
    Cidx_lfcmfr[i] <- UnoC(Surv.rsp = Surv_train, Surv.rsp.new = Surv_test, lpnew = risk_lfcmfr)
    Cidx_laft[i]   <- UnoC(Surv.rsp = Surv_train, Surv.rsp.new = Surv_test, lpnew = risk_laft)
    Cidx_lfcm[i]   <- UnoC(Surv.rsp = Surv_train, Surv.rsp.new = Surv_test, lpnew = risk_lfcm)
    
  }
  
  # ==========================================
  # FINAL RESULTS FOR CURRENT SETTING
  # ==========================================
  cat(sprintf("\n=== 10-Fold CV Results for %s (IPCW Integrated Brier Score) ===\n", setting_name))
  cat(sprintf("Mean lfAFT-fr IBS : %.4f (SD: %.4f)\n", mean(IBS_bayes, na.rm = TRUE), sd(IBS_bayes, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat(sprintf("Mean LFCM-fr IBS  : %.4f (SD: %.4f)\n", mean(IBS_lfcmfr, na.rm = TRUE), sd(IBS_lfcmfr, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat(sprintf("Mean lfAFT IBS    : %.4f (SD: %.4f)\n", mean(IBS_laft, na.rm = TRUE), sd(IBS_laft, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat(sprintf("Mean LFCM IBS     : %.4f (SD: %.4f)\n", mean(IBS_lfcm, na.rm = TRUE), sd(IBS_lfcm, na.rm = TRUE)))
  
  cat(sprintf("\n=== 10-Fold CV Results for %s (Uno's IPCW C-index) ===\n", setting_name))
  cat(sprintf("Mean lfAFT-fr C-idx : %.4f (SD: %.4f)\n", mean(Cidx_bayes, na.rm = TRUE), sd(Cidx_bayes, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat(sprintf("Mean LFCM-fr C-idx  : %.4f (SD: %.4f)\n", mean(Cidx_lfcmfr, na.rm = TRUE), sd(Cidx_lfcmfr, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat(sprintf("Mean lfAFT C-idx    : %.4f (SD: %.4f)\n", mean(Cidx_laft, na.rm = TRUE), sd(Cidx_laft, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat(sprintf("Mean LFCM C-idx     : %.4f (SD: %.4f)\n", mean(Cidx_lfcm, na.rm = TRUE), sd(Cidx_lfcm, na.rm = TRUE)))
}
```

```{r mgcv}
N <- nrow(data2) # number of samples
#Quadrature weights for Riemann integration
lvec <- matrix(1 / 1440, 1440, 1)
# matrix containing quadrature weights for all participants
L <- kronecker(matrix(1, N, 1),t(lvec))
# matrix containing functional domain values
S <- kronecker(matrix(1, N, 1), t(s_grid))
data2$S <- I(S)
#Pointwise product of w i(s) and the quadrature weights, "L"
data2$W_L <- I(data2$MIMS * L)
# Expand age into an N x 1440 matrix
data2$Age_mat <- I(matrix(data2$age, nrow = N, ncol = 1440))

# Create the interval-censored response matrix
y_aft <- matrix(log(data2$time), N, 2)
y_aft[, 2] <- y_aft[, 1]
y_aft[data2$event == 0, 2] <- Inf
data2$y_aft <- y_aft
X <- as.matrix(data$)

fit_mgcv <- gam(
  y_aft ~ age + BMI + gender + CHD +
    # te(S, Age_mat, by = W_L, bs = c("cc", "cr"), k = c(10, 5)) + 
    te(MIMS, S, by = L, bs = c("cr", "cc"), k = c(5, 5)) +
    s(STRAPSU, bs = "re"), 
  data = data2, 
  family = cnorm() 
)

fit <- gam(Y ~ age_in_years + bmi + ti(X, S, by = L, bs = c("cr", "cr"), k = c(20, 20), mc = c(TRUE, FALSE)), weights = delta, data = data2, family = cox.ph)

summary(fit_lfcm_mgcv)
gam.vcomp(fit_lfcm_mgcv)
```
